newsitem.title: POLAND: CURRENCY-SELLING MOOD, HIGH TUESDAY FIX LIFT ZLOTY.
newsitem.headline: CURRENCY-SELLING MOOD, HIGH TUESDAY FIX LIFT ZLOTY.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed against the basket of currencies on Wednesday amid light currency selling sentiment after players sold an estimated $100 at Tuesday's post-trade fixing, forex dealers said.
They said that today's currency-sales were mainly the result of the high Tuesday fixing and expectations that more currency sales may be in store.
"This morning trade was cautious after Tuesday's fixing but later trade normalised with some, mainly speculative, currency sales," said Maciek Grabosz, forex dealer at Bank Zachodni SA.
The zloty closed at 2.17/2.14 percent from the trading band centre, up from yesterday's 2.06/2.02 percent.
It closed at 2.8055/65 to the dollar, up from 2.8107/17 on Tuesday and at 1.8710/15 to the mark, down from 1.8705/15.
Dealers said that after the early jump in responce to Tuesday's fixing at an average of 2.18 percent from parity the zloty was relatively balanced for the rest of the session.

They said today's light dollar-selling sentiment may have been caused by players cutting currency positions to take advantage of Wednesday's value date, which is November 22, enabling them to store zlotys at higher rates for the weekend.
The central bank refrained from draining the money market on Wednesday despite slight overliquidity, which forced lenders to lower prices of short-term and mid-term deposits.
Overnight rates were at 18.50/18.70 percent, down from opening's 18.65/18.90 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 18.55/18.80 percent, down from 18.80/19.10 percent.
Three-month depos fell 0.1 point at bid to 19.40 percent.
Secondary T-bill market yields remained flat in thin trade, with the benchmark 52-week T-bill trading at 19.54/19.52 percent against last primary average yield of 19.53 percent.
